speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have a yellowish discoloration of your skin and eyes, which we call jaundice, along with some agitation. To help narrow down the cause, have you experienced any abdominal pain or noticed a change in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and substance use, have you experienced any fever, nausea, or dark urine recently? I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis or other infections. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Test

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Patient
text: protection. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That explanation doesn't align with your jaundice and agitation, so I must disregard it. Have you had any recent travel, consumed unpasteurized dairy, or experienced dark urine and pale stools? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Serology_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal liver function tests and hepatitis serology, we must look for other causes of jaundice and agitation, such as hemolysis or metabolic disorders. Have you noticed any muscle pain, weakness, or dark "cola-colored" urine, which might suggest rhabdomyolysis from your recent drug use? REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase_Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Since liver enzymes and muscle enzymes are normal, I need to rule out hemolysis, which can cause jaundice and neurological symptoms like agitation. Have you noticed any shortness of breath, fatigue, or dark urine that isn't related to muscle breakdown? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 16.3 g/dL, Hematocrit: 47%, Leukocyte Count: 9,750/mm3, Neutrophils: 58%, Bands: 2%, Eosinophils: 1%, Basophils: 0%, Lymphocytes: 24%, Monocytes: 2%, Platelet Count: 365,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: Your blood work is largely unremarkable, ruling out significant hemolysis or infection, so I need to investigate metabolic causes like Wilson's disease or acute porphyria. Have you noticed any abdominal pain, changes in mental status beyond agitation, or a family history of liver or neurological disorders? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Copper_and_Ceruloplasmin

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: With liver, hemolysis, and Wilson's disease ruled out, I suspect acute intermittent porphyria given your agitation and substance use history. Have you experienced darkening of your urine upon standing or exposure to light, and do you have a family history of similar episodes? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Porphobilinogen

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: With porphyria also ruled out, I suspect your symptoms are due to serotonin syndrome triggered by your recent ecstasy use. Do you currently have a fever, muscle rigidity, or involuntary muscle twitching? REQUEST TEST: Serum_Tryptophan_Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal tryptophan levels, serotonin syndrome is unlikely, so I must reconsider your jaundice and agitation in the context of your drug history. Have you experienced any recent weight loss, night sweats, or a cough, and have you noticed any bruising or bleeding tendencies? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: The coagulation panel shows a reduced prothrombin activity and elevated INR, which indicates impaired liver synthetic function despite the normal liver enzymes, suggesting acute liver failure. Given the history of ecstasy and cocaine use, this presentation is highly consistent with acute liver injury induced by these substances, particularly ecstasy. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute liver failure secondary to ecstasy and cocaine use
